title: The Measure of Faith and Diverse Gifts
english: He is being transformed. Having forewarned that God measures the measure of faith (Rom 12:3-8), he follows the preceding pattern and defends the one giving, persuading [us] not to be saddened if anyone has a lesser gift. For just as if there were a cheap part in a body, it is useful for everything, and the large and the small are apportioned into one body; for it is an induction from the former that we are members of one another. Those having diverse gifts [act] instead of the one having diverse gifts. The one giving in simplicity—that is, what the Lord says: give to everyone asking you, not seeking either good or evil and to whom you give (Luke 6:30)—since this precision often prevents us from giving to those to whom it ought to be given, the suspicion in us having erred many times.

It is worthy for those to be subject to kings who persevere in the service of the will of God (Rom 13:1), unless perhaps it is a hypothesis of persecutions in the midst; for concerning enduring all things through the faith.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
